title: Request Annotation Workbench: span linking, correlation timelines, and filter heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design an integrated "Request Annotation Workbench" for the Redwood Console that empowers engineers to inspect a single request end-to-end, annotate spans and events, and quickly pivot queries across correlation IDs, timeline slices, and filter heuristics. The goal is to reduce mean time to resolution for request-level incidents by making span relationships, causal edges, and KV/cache hits visible alongside contextual metadata and quick actions (jump-to-logs, open-PR, export-evidence).
acceptance_criteria: Workbench entrypoint accessible from trace list and request detail page
Visual timeline that aligns spans to request time and highlights inferred causal edges
Inline span annotation UX with tags and notes persisted to incident snapshots
Correlation-ID lane showing grouped requests and ability to pivot timeline to selected sibling
Filter heuristics panel that suggests high-value filters (latency > p95, kv-miss, model-fallback) based on sampled traces
Prototype validated with two engineering interviews and one on-call rotation test
Design spec includes accessibility considerations: keyboard nav, color contrast, and ARIA labels
design_notes: Primary constraints: preserve console performance (avoid heavy client-side rendering for long traces), support traces with 1000+ spans, and integrate with existing rollouts UI for canary/span level annotations. We propose a composable canvas: left column for timeline + span lane, right column for context cards (request meta, logs snapshot, model variant). Top toolbar contains quick filters and 'Capture Snapshot' action. Annotation model: ephemeral local notes until saved to incident snapshot to avoid accidental writes. Heuristics engine will surface 3 suggestions by default with option to expand to full list.
